$comment: Per-system deploy configuration. ONE GITHUB REPOSITORY PER SYSTEM SLUG.
Each system repository holds TWO folders:
real/  the customer-facing system  -> deployed into system/<slug>
demo/  the public demo             -> deployed into demo-systems/<slug>
They are different codebases kept as siblings, so ONE repository serves
both. A push to a system's repository therefore updates BOTH the real
system and its demo together; they cannot be deployed separately. This is
'cloneRoot': where the repositories are checked out on this machine. Each
system's checkout is '<cloneRoot>/<slug>'. The platform pulls the commit
there once and runs the real and demo builds from the two subfolders.
'repos' maps a system slug to its GitHub repository ('owner/repo'). A slug
with no entry is never deployed by a webhook.
'productionBranch' is the branch whose push triggers a deploy.
